Two persons were badly burnt and other properties destroyed when a fire outbreak occurred at the Amingo Gas Plant in Oraifite, Ekwusigo Local Government Area of Anambra State. It was gathered that the fire outbreak was triggered by an ignition from the engine of a gas tanker, resulting in a fire outbreak that affected a section of the gas plant, which occurred late on Sunday. Although no deaths were recorded, an eyewitness said the injured persons were immediately rushed to a nearby hospital for treatment. The eyewitness added that the fire raged for several minutes before operatives of the state fire service arrived and brought it under control. “The fire started suddenly at about 7:30 pm on Sunday with very thick smoke that engulfed the whole premises. It burnt several gas tanks at the location. The fire came with some explosions. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. We later learnt that the Inferno was triggered by an ignition from the engine of a gas tanker,” the eyewitness said. Confirming the incident in a statement on Monday, the Head of the Media and Publicity Unit of the Anambra State Fire Service, Chukwudi Chiketa, said firefighters were deployed immediately after receiving a distress call. He said, “The Anambra State Fire Service responded to a fire outbreak at Amingo Gas Plant, along Nkwo-to-Nkwo Road, Oraifite, in Ekwusigo Local Government Area of Anambra State. “The distress call was received at 1937 hours. Firefighting operations were successfully carried out, and the team withdrew from the scene at 2004 hours of the same day. “Preliminary reports indicate that the Inferno was triggered by an ignition from the engine of a gas tanker, resulting in a fire outbreak that affected a section of the gas plant. “Unfortunately, two staff members of the facility sustained injuries and were immediately taken to the hospital for medical attention.” Chiketa urged operators of gas plants, tanker drivers and other stakeholders in the petroleum and gas sector to strictly adhere to safety procedures. “Operators of gas plants, tanker drivers and other stakeholders in the petroleum and gas sector should ensure proper maintenance of vehicles and equipment, and avoid any activity that could trigger fire outbreaks around gas facilities. “Fire safety is everyone’s responsibility.
